section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection of the letter Yud to Eretz Yisrael through the two levels of fear of Heaven and the two levels of Chochmah.
section.t: And the explanation of the connection of the aspect of Yud to Eretz Yisrael
(that specifically in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with a Yud),
will be understood with an introduction from the teaching of the Maggid78
on the verse79
"A land which the L-rd your G-d cares for; the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are always upon it,"
for in the Zohar80
it asks: it is written81
"The eye of the L-rd is toward those who fear Him" in the singular, and it is written82
"The eyes of the L-rd are toward the righteous" in the plural.
And according to its simple meaning, it can be said that the wise are called83
"the eyes of the congregation."
And it is written84
"Chochmot (wisdoms) cries out in the street" — two wisdoms: the supernal Chochmah and the lower Chochmah.85
And there is an inner fear and an external fear. External fear is the fear that comes from greatness,86
meaning that one does not recognize His inner essence, but only sees His greatness, and because of this he is afraid.
[Similar to what is explained in Tanya,87
that even when one has never seen the king and does not know him at all, but only sees that many great ministers bow down to a certain person,
awe and dread will fall upon him.]
And inner fear is when one recognizes His inner essence and importance, and because of this he fears and is ashamed before Him.
And this fear is called "fear of shame."86
And these two aspects of fear correspond to the supernal Chochmah and the lower Chochmah.
For in the lower Chochmah,
which is the aspect of Malchus,
the fear there is from greatness,
and in the supernal Chochmah
(i.e., the aspect of Chochmah)
the fear is from inner essence.
And in order to have the fear of shame, one must recognize and comprehend His G-dliness,
and this is impossible except through a tzimtzum (contraction) in which He, as it were, contracts Himself so that He can be comprehended,
and this tzimtzum comes about when a person makes himself small, for "as water reflects a face back to a face."
And this is what is said regarding the Land of Israel: "the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are upon it" —
"eyes" in the plural,
meaning that in the Land of Israel there are two eyes,
the external fear and the inner fear.
For although "land" is the aspect of Malchus, the lower Chochmah,
nevertheless, due to the advantage of the returning light, there is also in it the revelation of the supernal fear.
This is analogous to how in the air close to the land there is more heat than in the middle air,
because the sun that strikes the land reflects illumination upward for a third of the space.
And this is "a land which the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are upon it" —
"land" is Eretz Yisrael,
and in it there are two eyes: the supernal Chochmah and the lower Chochmah.
"From the beginning of the year until the end of the year" —
"beginning" is the supernal Chochmah,
[and "beginning" is written deficiently (without an Aleph),
because the supernal Chochmah that is revealed in the lower Chochmah
(land)
does not have the Aleph that indicates the Supreme One.]
(This concludes the content of the teaching of the Maggid).
Based on this, it will be understood what they said: "Every Rav is from Bavel and every Rabbi is from Eretz Yisrael"
[that in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with the addition of a Yud, which indicates Chochmah],
for although Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of Malchus, the lower Chochmah and fear,
nevertheless,
since in the lower fear there is also a revelation of the supernal fear,
therefore in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with a Yud.
And this is also why the Yud that is added to "Rabi"
(from Eretz Yisrael)
is the aspect of the innerness of Chochmah, as above,
because the aspect of the fear of shame that comes from recognizing the inner essence is the aspect of the innerness of the supernal Chochmah,
and therefore the Yud in "Rabi"
(from Eretz Yisrael)
is the aspect of the innerness of Chochmah,
and even to the aspect of that which flows from Ein Sof,
as above from the Baal Shem Tov.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the ultimate bittul of Malchus, which must be applied in Torah, prayer, and charity to receive divine powers and achieve victory in the war against the evil inclination.
section.t: 8) And this is what is said by his holy honor, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, in the discourse regarding the Yud that is behind the Dalet,
that the letter Yud indicates bittul (self-nullification) and "az'eiarta d'garma" (self-diminution), and this is Malchus d'Atzilus, which has nothing of its own,
for the bittul of the aspect of Malchus is
[not only the bittul of "az'eiarta d'garma,"
but rather]
the aspect of bittul of "having nothing of its own,"
which is the ultimate bittul.
And as above, that specifically in Malchus,
the aspect of the lower Chochmah,
the most supreme aspect of bittul is revealed.
And he continues in the discourse,
that this bittul must be in all three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness,
for in the study of Torah, mere bittul is insufficient
(the negation of coarseness of spirit),
rather it must be "in the aspect of utter self-nullification,"
and likewise in the line of service
(prayer)
there must be the bittul of "I am poor and needy," which is the aspect of the bittul of Malchus,
and likewise in the line of acts of kindness
(fulfillment of the commandments)
he explains with the analogy of lifting a heavy burden
(which is an analogy for the matter of fulfilling the commandments,
as above),
that in order to lift an extremely heavy burden
(it is not enough to contract oneself a little,
but rather)
one must contract oneself greatly.
And through this bittul
(in all three lines mentioned above)
he becomes an empty vessel that can contain,
receiving all the revelations and powers that are given from above to perform his service in Torah study, fulfillment of the commandments, and the service of prayer,
and even to the point that he makes the connection and falsehood of the world transform into the planks of the Mishkan,
transforming the foolishness of idolatry into the foolishness of holiness.
For all this is through the bittul of an empty vessel,
for then he is a vessel to receive the powers given from above so that he can overcome the war against the evil inclination,
as explained in the discourse88
that for the sake of overcoming the war, they expend the hidden treasures from generation to generation
(what he himself stored up and also what his ancestors stored up)
and they are delivered through the officers of the army,
specifically for the men of the army
(the men of the army)
who actually bring about the victory,
"the hosts of the L-rd,"
in all three interpretations of this,
as explained in the discourse.89
And the title "the hosts of the L-rd" for Israel began from the time of the Exodus from Egypt,
as it is written,90
"On that very day,
all the hosts of the L-rd went out of the land of Egypt,"
and from this it is also understood regarding the future redemption,
that it will be similar to the redemption from Egypt, as it is written,91
"As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
through which there will be the revelation of the future redemption, when there will be wonders even relative to the matters that were in the Exodus from Egypt,92
and afterwards there will be "awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust,"93
and He is among them.
